verses.sanskrit:
विदुर उवाच।
              शकुनीनामिहार्थाय पाशं भूमावयोजयत्। कश्चिच्छाकुनिकस्तात पूर्वेषामिति शुश्रुम ॥१॥
verses.english: Vidura said For the capture of birds did a certain fowler set his net in this world. O Sire, so we have heard from old men.
verses.bhavadeepa: तान्येवाह - क्षमा परेभ्यः ताडनादिप्राप्तावपि संतापानुदयः । धृतिः- कामादिभिरननुतप्तता अहिंसा- वाङ्मनःशरीरैः परस्य पीडाया अकरणम् । समता- शत्रुमित्रादौ तुल्यत्वम् । सत्यं- यथार्थभाषणम् । आर्जवम्- अकौटिल्यम् । इन्द्रियाणां जयः धैर्यम् अत्यन्तापद्यपि मनसोऽवैक्लव्यम् । मार्दवं - प्रियवादिता । ह्रीरकार्यान्निवृत्तिः । अचापलं - स्थैर्यं वाड्मनःकायानाम् । एते दान्तानां गुणाः ॥१४॥

verses.sanskrit: तस्मिंस्तौ शकुनौ बद्धौ युगपत्सहचारिणौ। तावुपादाय तं पाशं जग्मतुः खचरावुभौ ॥२॥
verses.english: There were two birds, companions to each other, captured in that net and they both went up into the air with that net.
verses.bhavadeepa: दमस्य श्रेष्ठ्यं प्रतिपाद्यादान्तयोः कलहं कुर्वतोर्द्वयोरपि नाश इति प्रतिपादयन्नाख्यायिकामुखेनाह - शकुनीनामिति । पूर्वेषां मुखात् ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: तौ विहाय समाक्रान्तौ दृष्ट्वा शाकुनिकस्तदा। अन्वधावद‌निर्विण्णो येन येन स्म गच्छतः ॥३॥
verses.english: The fowler seeing them fly up in the air without losing his senses followed them in the direction they took.

verses.sanskrit: तथा तमनुधावन्तं मृगयुं शकुनार्थिनम्। आश्रमस्थो मुनिः कश्चिद्ददर्शाथ कृताह्निकः ॥४॥
verses.english: A certain Rishi living in a hermitage, who had finished his daily worship I saw that fowler following the birds, still in the hope of getting hold of the birds.

verses.sanskrit: तावन्तरिक्षगौ शीघ्रमनुयान्तं महीचरम्। श्लोकेनानेन कौरव्य पप्रच्छ स मुनिस्तदा ॥५॥
verses.english: Then did the anchoring address, O Kauravya, that denizen of the earth following the wanderers of the sky in this couplet.

verses.sanskrit: विचित्रमिदमाश्चर्यं मृगहन् प्रतिभाति मे। प्लवमानौ हि खचरौ पदातिरनुधावसि ॥६॥
verses.english: Slayer of animals, it seems to me wonderfully strange that you who move by your feet in this earth are following wanderers of the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
शाकुनिक उवाच।
              पाशमेकमुभावेतौ सहितौ हरतो मम। यत्र वै विवदिष्येते तत्र मे वशमेष्यतः ॥७॥
verses.english: The fowler said These two united are taking that one net of mine but they will come under my control where they will quarrel.

verses.sanskrit:
विदुर उवाच।
              तौ विवादमनुप्राप्तौ शकुनौ मृत्युसन्धितौ। विगृह्य च सुदुर्बुद्धी पृथिव्यां सन्निपेततुः ॥८॥
verses.english: Vidura said The two birds who were doomed to death quarreled; and having quarrelled the two fools fell to the earth.

verses.sanskrit: तौ युध्यमानौ संरब्धौ मृत्युपाशवशानुगौ। उपसृत्यापरिज्ञातो जग्राह मृगहा तदा ॥९॥
verses.english: The slayer of animals then approaching those two fighting with each other, subject to the trap of death, without their knowledge caught hold of them.

verses.sanskrit: एवं ये ज्ञातयोऽर्थेषु मिथो गच्छन्ति विग्रहम्। तेऽमित्रवशमायान्ति शकुनाविव विग्रहात् ॥१०॥
verses.english: In the same way those cousins who quarrel in matters of wealth are brought under the control of enemies like the birds owing to their quarrel.

verses.sanskrit: सम्भोजनं सङ्कथनं  संप्रश्नोऽथ समागमः। एतानि ज्ञातिकार्याणि न विरोधः कदाचन ॥११॥
verses.english: Dining in one another's company and conversing among, one another, inquiring about one another's health and living together, these are the duties of cousins and quarrel is never.

verses.sanskrit: ये स्म काले सुमनसः सर्वे वृद्धानुपासते। सिंहगुप्तमिवारण्यमप्रधृष्या भवन्ति ते ॥१२॥
verses.english: Those who in proper season serve the old men out of pure motives, become invincible like a forest protected by lions.

verses.sanskrit: येऽर्थं सन्ततमासाद्य दीना इव समासते। श्रियं ते संप्रयच्छन्ति द्विषद्भ्यो भरतर्षभ ॥१३॥
verses.english: Those, who attaining to prosperity behave like the mean-minded contribute to the prosperity of their despisers, O you bull among the race of Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: धूमायन्ते व्यपेतानि ज्वलन्ति सहितानि च। धृतराष्ट्रोल्मुकानीव ज्ञातयो भरतर्षभ ॥१४॥
verses.english: Cousins, O you bull among the race of Bharata, smoke when quarrelling and blaze up when like charcoals.

verses.sanskrit: इदमन्यत् प्रवक्ष्यामि यथा दृष्टं गिरौ मया। श्रुत्वा तदपि कौरव्य यथा श्रेयस्तथा कुरु ॥१५॥
verses.english: or I shall speak of something else, which was seen by me in a mountain and hearing that too, O son of Kuru, do whatever is good.

verses.sanskrit: वयं किरातैः सहिता गच्छामो गिरिमुत्तरम्। ब्राह्मणैर्देवकल्पैश्च विद्याजम्भकवार्तिकैः ॥१६॥
verses.english: We want to the Northern mountains accompanied by hunters and godlike Brahmanas fond of conversations incantations and medicines.

verses.sanskrit: कुञ्जभूतं गिरिं सर्वमभितो गन्धमादनम्। दीप्यमानौषधिगणं सिद्धगन्धर्वसेवितम् ॥१७॥
verses.english: The Gandhamadana mountain was like a grove (owing to tress growing on it) in every way. It was shining, as it were, with cluster of medicinal plants and inhabited by ascetics and the Gandharvas,
verses.bhavadeepa: विद्याजंभकवार्तिकाः विद्या मन्त्रयंत्रादिरूपा जंभक औषधीसाधनानि तद्वार्ताप्रियाः विद्याजंभकवार्तिकाः ॥१६॥

verses.sanskrit: तत्रापश्याम वै सर्वे मधुपीतकमाक्षिकम्। मरुप्रपाते विषमे निविष्टं कुम्भसम्मितम् ॥१८॥
verses.english: There we all saw some honey of a yellow colour inside a pot placed at a very high point of the mountain.

verses.sanskrit: आशीविषै रक्ष्यमाणं कुबेरदयितं भृशम्। यत्प्राप्य पुरुषो मत्यर्थोऽप्यमरत्वं नियच्छति ॥१९॥
verses.english: This was guarded by snakes, the favourite drink of Kubera, as it was drinking which even an earthy man gets immortality.

verses.sanskrit: अचक्षुर्लभते चक्षुर्वृद्धो भवति वै युवा। इति ते कथयन्ति स्म ब्राह्मणा जम्भसाधकाः ॥२०॥
verses.english: Those without eyes get eyes, and the old become young. There was the honey described by the Brahmanas conversant with incantations.

verses.sanskrit: ततः किरातास्तद्दृष्ट्वा प्रार्थयन्तो महीपते। विनेशुर्विषमे तस्मिन् ससर्पे गिरिगह्वरे ॥२१॥
verses.english: Then did the hunters, seeing that strive to obtain it, О king and were destroyed in thai frightful mountain cavern full of snakes.

verses.sanskrit: तथैव तव पुत्रोऽयं पृथिवीमेक इच्छति। मधु पश्यति सम्मोहात् प्रपातं नानुपश्यति ॥२२॥
verses.english: Thus does this son of yours desire to be the one supreme individual in this world; out of loss of his senses, does he see only the honey and not the fall.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनो योद्धमनाः समरे सव्यसाचिना। न च पश्यामि तेजोऽस्य विक्रमं वा तथाविधम् ॥२३॥
verses.english: Duryodhana is desirous of a fight with Savyasachin; but I do not see in him the strength or energy necessary for that purpose.

verses.sanskrit: एकेन रथमास्थाय पृथिवी येन निर्जिता। भीष्मद्रोणप्रभृतयः सन्त्रस्ताः साधुयायिनः ॥२४॥
verses.english: That Savyasachin, who alone in his car has brought the earth under his control and who inspired dared into Bhishma, Drona and others accompanied by their hosts.

verses.sanskrit: विराटनगरे भग्नाः किं तत्र तव दृश्यताम्। प्रतीक्षमाणो यो वीरः क्षमते वीक्षितं तव ॥२५॥
verses.english: They were routed at the city of Virata-sce what occurred there. That hero looking at your face and waiting to see your movements will forgive you still.

verses.sanskrit: द्रुपद्रो मत्स्यराजश्च संक्रुद्धश्च धनञ्जयः। न शेषयेयुः समरे वायुयुक्ता इवाग्नयः ॥२६॥
verses.english: Drupada, the king of the Matsyas and Dhananjaya, fired with wrath, will leave no trace (of your army) like a conflagration urged on by the wind.
verses.bhavadeepa: तव दृश्यतां त्वया द्रष्टव्यं बलमिति शेषः । यो वीरः कर्णादिः ॥२५॥

verses.sanskrit: अङ्के कुरुष्व राजानं धृतराष्ट्र युधिष्ठिरम्। युध्यतोर्हि द्वयोर्युद्धे नैकान्तेन भवेज्जयः ॥२७॥
verses.english: 0 Dhritarashtra, take the king Yudhishthira on your lap; for by a struggle between you two none can get an absolute victory.
